overview.title: Index: D to G (distributed training to GPUs)
overview.main_topic: Index entries from the end of 'diffusion models' to 'GPUs'
overview.central_idea: This page finishes D (distributed training, dropout) and covers E (early stopping, Embedding layer, encoder), F (feature engineering, fit(), Functional API, float8/float16) and the start of G (generalization, Gemma, GPT).
overview.importance: It points to the generalization chapter, the Keras fit()/Functional API material and the scaling and precision techniques.
learning_objectives: Find the generalization, dropout and early-stopping pages
Find how to customize fit() with JAX, PyTorch or TensorFlow

summary:
Index page printed 612 (PDF 636). Locators are **printed** pages: **add 24** for the PDF page.

**D (end).** The *diffusion models* sub-entries continue: training process 525, U-Net denoising autoencoder 522 (PDF 546). Then *distance function* 585, *distributed training* 551–555 (PDF 575–579) with DeviceMesh API 552 and LayoutMap API 553–555, *Dogs vs. Cats dataset* 242 (PDF 266), *dot-product attention* 439 (PDF 463), *dropout* 167–168 (PDF 191–192) and *Dropout layer* 168, 215, 254.

**E.** *early stopping* 161, 209, 400, 544 (PDF 185, 233, 424, 568). *Einsum notation* 439. *Embedding layer* 410–424, 452 (PDF 434). *embeddings, word* 409, 410 (PDF 433). *encoder* 444, 455, 464. *evaluate()* 191, 203, 230. *evaluation protocol, choosing* 181. *expert systems* 3, 14. *extreme generalization* 573, 594 (PDF 597).

**F.** *feature engineering* 10, 159, 181 (PDF 34, 183, 205). *feature maps* 236. *few-shot learning* 470 (PDF 494). *fit()* 191, 223, 342, 489 (PDF 215, 247), with customizing via JAX 225, PyTorch 224 and TensorFlow 223. *float8 training* 560, *float16 inference* 558, *floating-point precision* 557. *forward pass* 40 (PDF 64). *Functional API* 192, 195 (PDF 216, 219), with multi-input, multi-output models 197–198 and feature extraction 200.

**G.** *generalization* 137–148 (PDF 161–172): local vs. extreme 573, nature of 143–148, underfitting and overfitting 137–142. *Gemma model* 485–488 (PDF 509–512). *generate()* 486–535. *generative AI* 596. *GlobalAveragePooling2D* 234, 245. *Google Colab* 17 (PDF 41). *GPT* 469 (PDF 493).

concepts.name: generalization (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 137–148 (PDF 161–172). Sub-entries: underfitting and overfitting 137–142, nature of 143–148, local vs. extreme 573, spectrum of 576.
concepts.intuition: Chapter 5's machine-learning fundamentals start at PDF 161. The later sub-entries are the chapter 19 view.
concepts.technical: Related entries: extreme generalization 573, 594; broad generalization 576.
concepts.significance: Generalization is the book's central goal for machine learning.
concepts.example: Open PDF 167 for the nature of generalization (printed 143).
concepts.misconception: Generalization is not the same as a low training loss.

concepts.name: Functional API (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 192, 195 (PDF 216, 219). Sub-entries: multi-input, multi-output models 197–198, plotting layer connectivity 199, feature extraction 200.
concepts.intuition: This is where the book shows how to build models as graphs of layers.
concepts.technical: Neighbouring entries: fit() 191 and evaluate() 191 at PDF 215.
concepts.significance: Most of the book's advanced models are built with the Functional API.
concepts.misconception: The Functional API is not limited to linear stacks of layers.

concepts.name: dropout (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 167–168 (PDF 191–192). The Dropout layer is also at 215 and 254, and recurrent dropout is listed under R.
concepts.intuition: PDF 191 is the regularization section of chapter 5.
concepts.technical: The 'argument 215, 373' sub-entry covers the training flag and the RNN dropout argument.
concepts.significance: It is one of the main ways the book fights overfitting.
concepts.misconception: Dropout is applied only during training.
